evidence: Cic. Att. 7.12.1: velim mihi ignōscās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With the dative of the person and the accusative of the thing: ignōsce mihi, forgive me (see excuse me).
Classically to send away, let go; the Vulgate’s verb for forgiving debts and sins and the people who owe them (dīmitte nōbīs dēbita nostra, the Lord’s Prayer).
Of sins: quōrum remīseritis peccāta, remittuntur eīs (Jo. 20.23).

phrases.latin: sīc ignōvisse putātō mē tibi, sī cēnās hodiē mēcum
phrases.english: consider yourself forgiven, if you dine with me today
To err is human, to forgive divine.

phrases.latin: Domine, quotiēs peccābit in mē frāter meus, et dīmittam eī? ūsque septiēs?
phrases.english: Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him? As many as seven times?

phrases.latin: Sī peccāverit in tē frāter tuus, increpā illum: et sī poenitentiam ēgerit, dīmitte illī.
phrases.english: If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
